flawed_step: The only order-independent bound greedy satisfies is Delta(G)+1 (a vertex has at most Delta coloured neighbours). No step can connect this to chi(G)+1: for bipartite graphs chi=2 while Delta, and the greedy count under a bad order, can be arbitrarily large.
counterexample: Crown graph on 8 vertices: a1..a4, b1..b4, with ai~bj iff i != j (K_{4,4} minus a perfect matching). Bipartite with edges, so chi=2 and chi+1=3. Order a1,b1,a2,b2,a3,b3,a4,b4. a1 gets 1. b1 (not adjacent to a1) gets 1. a2 (sees b1=1) gets 2. b2 (sees a1=1) gets 2. a3 (sees b1=1, b2=2) gets 3. b3 (sees a1=1, a2=2) gets 3. a4 (sees b1,b2,b3 = 1,2,3) gets 4. b4 (sees a1,a2,a3 = 1,2,3) gets 4. Greedy uses 4 colours, and 4 > 3.
assessment_summary: The statement is false. Greedy is only guaranteed to use at most Delta+1 colours. On the crown graph K_{4,4} minus a perfect matching (chi=2), the order a1,b1,...,a4,b4 forces 4 colours, more than chi+1=3. On K_{n,n} minus a perfect matching the same order forces n colours.
